questions.title: Bootstrap particle likelihood estimation and nonlinear filtering
questions.description: Develop a complete source-assisted research analysis of bootstrap particle filtering at a fixed finite observation horizon. In persistent Markdown/LaTeX, define the hidden-state model, filtering and unnormalized Feynman-Kac measures and normalizing constant; specify initialization, multinomial resampling before each subsequent transition, propagation, weighting and likelihood accumulation. Derive the exact finite-N unbiasedness of the unnormalized particle measure and likelihood estimator by conditional expectation, without assuming independent likelihood increments. Derive fixed-horizon consistency for bounded test functions under explicit sufficient assumptions; distinguish this from a growing-horizon theorem or an assertion about unbounded posterior moments. Demonstrate why normalized filtering estimates and log likelihood estimates are not generally unbiased, and state what logarithmic numerical stabilization does and does not change. Apply the framework to a finite Gaussian-emission HMM and a nonlinear stochastic-volatility model, auditing their assumptions and any limitations. Reproduce the complete pinned particles book experiment for stochastic volatility: three filters, 250 runs each at N=1000, the first 201 GBP/USD observations, and its N=65536 SQMC benchmark and figure. Report actual results, warnings, environment and source identity; do not call its SQMC benchmark exact or claim the entire book was reproduced. Implement the public bootstrap-filter interface with model-authored Python, using NumPy/SciPy primitives if useful, without substituting an exact filter or a prebuilt particle-filter call for the requested generated implementation. Exploratory computation should challenge theory and code. Obtain independent review of the exact current theory and implementation. Freeze a confirmatory experiment with at least one informative finite-HMM observation sequence and one informative stochastic-volatility sequence, two particle counts with the larger at least four times the smaller, and at least 1000 independent particle-system runs per model and count. Compare likelihood estimates, log-likelihood estimates and bounded filtering-event probabilities to independently validated exact or converged numerical references. Report bias with Monte Carlo uncertainty, likelihood relative MCSE at most 0.02, variance versus particle count, ESS and numerical failures; use the correct conditional-on-observations replication unit. Freeze seeds, precision, thresholds and stopping before outcomes and report all unmet criteria. Bind source reproduction, reviewable derivations, generated code, independent review and actual confirmation into a final research report with remaining gaps. Formalization and novelty are not required. This is not the consumed exact linear-Gaussian recursion task, parameter inference, smoothing, PMCMC, or the growing-horizon lognormal CLT.

source.primary_authority: Chopin and Papaspiliopoulos (2020), An Introduction to Sequential Monte Carlo, DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-47845-2. Computational reproduction uses particles 0.4 at f71e94a21a11c73b58e2d694775b1b1d379b8854, book Section 10.4.2/Figure 10.3 script. Berard, Del Moral and Doucet (2014), DOI 10.1214/EJP.v19-3428, supplies additional normalizing-constant context, not a demand to rederive its growing-horizon theorem.
source.hidden_gold: Independent referee controls, numerical oracles and outcomes remain evaluator-only.

request_fields.name: model
request_fields.edge_cases: The latent HMM state is its zero-based integer index, not its emission mean.

request_fields.name: parameters
request_fields.meaning: For gaussian_hmm: initial (probability vector), transition (row-stochastic matrix), means and scales (Gaussian emission parameters), all in state-index order. For stochastic_volatility: mu, rho, sigma, with X0 stationary Gaussian, Xt=mu+rho*(Xprevious-mu)+sigma*standard_normal and Yt conditional on Xt distributed N(0, exp(Xt)).
request_fields.shape: HMM has 2 to 5 states, nonnegative probabilities and positive scales. Stochastic volatility has abs(rho)<1 and sigma>0.
request_fields.units: Scales and sigma are standard deviations; exp(Xt) is observation variance.
request_fields.indexing: An observation is associated with the initial state X0 before any transition.
request_fields.edge_cases: HMM initial/transition probabilities may include zero. Supplied parameters are known, not estimated.

request_fields.name: observations
request_fields.meaning: Ordered finite scalar observations y0 through y(T-1).
request_fields.shape: Length 1 to 256; evaluated stochastic-volatility observations are nonzero.
request_fields.edge_cases: Do not sort, discard or refit observations. Long low-density sequences require stable log-domain accumulation.

request_fields.name: particles
request_fields.meaning: Number N of particles, constant through the run.
request_fields.edge_cases: N=1 is a valid diagnostic request.

request_fields.name: seed
request_fields.meaning: Seed controlling the particle algorithm's randomization, not the observation sequence.
request_fields.edge_cases: Identical requests must reproduce within the implementation; no particular RNG family or exact draw ordering is required.

request_fields.name: threshold
request_fields.meaning: Threshold c for the bounded filtering event Xt<=c.
request_fields.indexing: Same threshold at all observation times.
request_fields.edge_cases: HMM event uses state indices; stochastic-volatility event uses latent log variance.

response_fields.name: log_normalizers
response_fields.meaning: Cumulative logarithm of the particle likelihood estimate after each observation.
response_fields.indexing: Element t includes observations 0 through t.
response_fields.edge_cases: This is the log of the product of average unnormalized weights, not the sum of log normalized weights, a filtering normalizer reset each step, or a claim of unbiased log likelihood.
response_fields.normalization: Divide each incremental sum of unnormalized bootstrap weights by N.

response_fields.name: filtered_means
response_fields.meaning: Weighted empirical expectation of the current latent state before resampling for the next observation.
response_fields.edge_cases: These are finite-particle estimates, not generally exact or unbiased; an unbounded-moment consistency claim needs its own assumptions.

response_fields.name: filtered_events
response_fields.meaning: Weighted empirical probability of Xt<=threshold after each observation.
response_fields.normalization: Normalized current weights applied to the indicator.

response_fields.name: ess
response_fields.meaning: Weight-based effective sample size after weighting and before the next resampling.
response_fields.shape: T scalars in [1,N], up to roundoff.
response_fields.edge_cases: This is a diagnostic, not an independent effective number of samples or proof of accuracy.
response_fields.normalization: Reciprocal of the sum of squared normalized weights.

response_fields.name: converged
response_fields.meaning: The requested numerical run produced resolved finite outputs.
response_fields.edge_cases: Unresolved numerical failure must not be reported as success.
response_fields.normalization: Execution status only, not a scientific validity verdict.

invariants.meaning: Use bootstrap propagation and multinomial resampling before every transition after time zero, with exactly N particles. Do not substitute a deterministic exact filter, guided proposal, adaptive resampling scheme or prebuilt filtering implementation. Numerical primitives are allowed and reuse must be disclosed.
Do not mutate supplied inputs or use undeclared data. Added output fields are allowed.
Only valid requests are evaluated; no hidden malformed-input taxonomy or exact random-stream match is required. Equivalent implementations are compared numerically and distributionally.

empirical_claims.meaning: Use both model families, at least two particle counts separated by a factor of at least four, and at least 1000 independent particle systems per model/count at fixed informative observations. Freeze all criteria and seeds before confirmation; likelihood relative MCSE must be <=0.02.

Assess likelihood bias relative to a validated reference with Monte Carlo uncertainty, log-likelihood bias, and variance versus N. A finite sample mean may lie above its population mean; do not confuse log bias with likelihood bias.

Assess bounded-event filtering error, Monte Carlo uncertainty, ESS and numerical failures. Validate numerical reference convergence for nonlinear filtering, rather than treating a single particle system as exact.

Independent particle-system runs at fixed data test a conditional-on-observations property. Report failures and limitations; finite experiments do not prove unbiasedness, universal variance rates or every unbounded posterior-moment claim.

estimator_execution_contract.termination_guarantee: Finite-horizon computation with honest numerical status; no prescribed derivation length, tool-use count or revision sequence.
